The oldest company on earth was nearly killed by debt 🏯

Kongō Gumi was founded in Japan in the year 578 and built the country's temples for about 40 generations of the same family. It survived wars, earthquakes and the rise and fall of empires. Then came borrowing: debts piled up from Japan's 1980s property bubble, and in 2006 the company had to be sold to save the business.

1,400 years of survival, undone by debt. 👀
